findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer never states the two tables agree omits the general chapter's pointer and the persistent-variability procedure and instead resolves the question by picking a document — "the chapter specific to your situation (A6.8 for a multiparameter sonde and A6.1–A6.7 for individual parameters) takes precedence over general guidance" — which is the prohibited way of resolving the imagined conflict. Unmet: States plainly that the two tables give the same stabilisation criteria and do not conflict; States the general field-measurement chapter itself points multiparameter users to the multiparameter chapter for criteria of the same kind; States the criteria are standard sensor stabilisation criteria and that actual sensor accuracy varies by model and manufacturer which is a separate matter; For persistent variability extends equilibration and records additional measurements then reports the median of the final five or more readings or selects a representative final reading with documented judgment

scored 0 — The answer refuses the cross-sensor sequencing question and makes none of the required points about order temperature first conductivity before pH ionic-strength rationale triple DIW rinses or pre-use calibration checks. Unmet: states the order does matter and gives temperature first; gives specific conductance next before pH; gives the general remaining order as pH DO ORP turbidity then ion-selective and fluorescence sensors with the A6.2 two-point DO exception; explains the rationale as working from low to high ionic strength; states conductivity must be calibrated before pH because pH buffers are high in ionic strength; states the sensors are rinsed three times with deionized water between standards; states the sonde is calibrated or checked before each field use

scored 0 — The answer refuses the question outright giving none of the required values (9.09 9.06 0.03 mg/L) no Benson and Krause attribution no comparison of the difference against the ±0.2 mg/L tolerance and no advice on which table to use. Unmet: gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; States the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure; notes the USGS values are generated from the Benson and Krause equations; Compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently

scored 0 — The answer gives the multiplication method and cites table 6.2–4 but withholds the required factor 0.8235 saying it lacks the information which is a refusal of a figure the rubric asks for. Unmet: Gives 0.8235 as the factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm

scored 0 — The answer approves diluting commercial standards (including StablCal) and recommends dilution as consistent with procedures violating the must-not item and it makes none of the required points. Unmet: states that commercial calibration solutions must not be diluted; gives 4 000-unit formazin as the one exception that may be diluted; explains that diluting changes the suspension matrix so the dilutions are no longer linear; recommends buying commercially prepared solutions at the values needed rather than preparing them by dilution

scored 0 — The answer misses every ordering point (no temperature-first no conductance-before-pH no ionic-strength rationale) and violates the must-nots by placing pH before specific conductance and treating the remaining order as unconstrained. Unmet: States order matters and gives a recommended sequence; Places temperature first in the sequence; Places specific conductance before pH; Places dissolved oxygen and then ORP after pH; Explains the sequence runs from lower to higher ionic strength to avoid carryover bias; Notes pH buffers and electrode filling solutions are high ionic strength and would contaminate a conductivity calibration

scored 0 — The answer is a bare refusal that withholds the substantive content the rubric expects (drift-rate absence turbidity fouling check EPA SOP pre/post-calibration and default criteria and the pass-or-fail/qualification distinction) making at most the first point. Unmet: States that no source gives an allowable rate of drift - a per-day or per-week figure - for a sensor left in the water; States that it gives no procedure for correcting or adjusting a record after the instrument comes out; Notes that the turbidity chapter does offer a fouling check comparing the sensor's reading on a calibrant before and after cleaning it and taking the percent difference; States that this fouling check quantifies one sensor's condition and is not an acceptance rule for the record; Notes that the EPA field calibration SOP has the operator calibrate before deployment and check the calibration on recovery defers the drift criteria to the project's quality assurance plan and supplies its own default post-calibration criteria only for when that plan is silent; Declines to convert the EPA post-calibration criteria into a keep-or-discard threshold for a month of record and supplies no drift tolerance beyond them; Notes that the EPA SOP's default post-calibration criteria are a pass-or-fail check on the instrument at recovery not a rule for how much of the record may be kept and that data failing the check are qualified rather than discarded
